method_corrections_made_mid_leg: The headline counts ONLY pins whose OWN targeted mutation left them green. An earlier framing ('did any of N mutations ever turn this pin red') would have scored every pin no mutation aimed at as a decoration and inflated the number badly; that framing was rejected.

Control and mutated runs must differ ONLY in the mutation. The first implementation ran the control on the TARGET subset but judged the mutation on the FULL 184-pin set - an asymmetric experiment that produced two FALSE 'SURVIVED' verdicts (M8/TestParentKeyConvergence, M14/creates_internal_nodes). Both were hand-checked, both died when their own mutation was run against their own targets, and the instrument was fixed rather than the verdicts accepted. See H2b-F3.
Every edit asserts its anchor occurs EXACTLY ONCE and that the file bytes changed on disk. A mutation that silently fails to apply is indistinguishable from a pin that detected nothing.
Restore is byte-exact (read_bytes/write_bytes). Text-mode restore re-translated newlines on Windows and produced a false RESTORE FAILED on a file that was never really changed.

findings.summary: Instruction-level read-only fences do not hold. THREE separate delegated attempts at Part A ended with agents editing shared source in the orchestrator's worktree despite an explicit, repeated, reasoned READ-ONLY instruction. Attempt 1: an assayer built its own mutation harness and mutated live tool source while ten sibling agents were probing the same tree. Attempts 2 and 3: agents edited tests/conftest.py, tests/test_lop_flywheel.py and tests/test_m3_logs_doctor.py, and re-ran a mutation harness - in one case while holding an absolute path to a tree they had been told explicitly not to touch. Each attempt was discarded and the tree restored.
findings.consequence: Part A could not be delegated and was executed directly by the orchestrator. Constitution Article V already requires 'every parallel agent gets its own git worktree' - the first attempt violated that and it is the orchestrator's error, but attempts 2 and 3 HAD isolation and still leaked.
findings.recommendation: the fence must be structural (a tool-permission deny, as harness/agent-settings.json already does for its own files), not prose in a prompt. Prose is advisory to a model; a deny-list is not.

findings.anchor: git worktree list during run wf_cce57a2d-980
findings.summary: The Workflow tool's `isolation: 'worktree'` created all eleven agent worktrees at f90946d - that is master / v5.34.0, NOT the orchestrator's branch HEAD. Verified: `git merge-base --is-ancestor c0cc415 f90946d` is false, and tests/test_hou_reimport_guard.py is absent there.
findings.consequence: Every agent in that run probed a tree WITHOUT the RES fix, i.e. with the fake-hou residency live - precisely the condition the brief forbids as uninterpretable. The entire run was discarded on that ground alone, independently of the intrusion in H2b-F1.
findings.recommendation: an isolated worktree must be pinned to the dispatching branch's HEAD, and the agent must verify its own base before probing. This leg's working method - orchestrator creates the worktrees itself at a named SHA and asserts a fix-marker file exists in each before dispatch - is the pattern that worked.

findings.summary: My own mutation instrument produced two FALSE 'surviving-mutation' verdicts before it was corrected. The control ran the TARGET subset while the mutated run used the FULL 184-pin set; under composition M8 and M14 did not surface, so two live pins were scored as decorations. Hand-running each mutation against its own targets killed both (M8 -> 3 failures, M14 -> 1 failure).
findings.consequence: Had this shipped uncorrected the headline surviving-mutation count would have been 5 instead of 3, and two healthy pins would have been libelled as decorations. It is the same class of defect this leg exists to find, occurring inside the instrument built to find it.
findings.recommendation: control and treatment must differ in exactly one variable. Adopted: the matrix now judges every mutation on the same subset its control ran, and uses the full-set run only to observe collateral.

findings.summary: A mutation row with TWO edits to the same file overwrote its own saved original with the already-mutated bytes, so the restore left the first edit in the tree. Caught by the post-run `git diff` gate, NOT by the restore's own sha assertion - that assertion compared against the corrupted baseline and passed.
findings.consequence: one row (M21) left set_purpose.py modified; detected, fixed, re-run clean.
findings.recommendation: a self-check that validates against a value the same bug can corrupt is not a check. The external `git diff HEAD` gate is what caught it and should stay.

findings.summary: F8's NAMED HARM SURVIVES ITS OWN REPAIR. The parent-key divergence is fixed - all three parent-taking tools share PARENT_KEYS - but _resolve_parent_path still falls through to '/stage' for any unrecognised key. Live: component_builder.execute({'asset_name': ..., 'parentPath': <lopnet>}) raises nothing and builds into /stage, exactly the silent misdirection F8 described. Note import_megascans DOES reject unknown keys (validate raises 'unknown parameter(s)'), so the family is inconsistent in the half that matters.
findings.why_it_matters: F8 was filed LOW because the naming looked cosmetic; the silent default was the real defect and it is still live in at least one tool. A caller with a typo gets a component in the wrong network and a success status.
findings.disposition: reported, not repaired - this leg measures.

findings.summary: The pin asserts len(geo.points()) > 0 to prove the .usdc reached the SOP chain. Live, a 4-point mesh fixture cooks to ONE point, because usdimport produces a packed USD prim rather than unpacked geometry. The assertion passes, but it reads as 'the geometry arrived' when what it proves is 'a packed prim exists'. It is not a decoration - M2 kills it - but it is weaker than its wording.

for_ruling.question: The three surviving-mutation pins: repair, retarget, or retire?
for_ruling.context: test_megascans_material_reference_is_orphaned (F3), test_variant_set_reaches_the_terminal (F5) and test_variant_materials_are_wired_statically (F4) all assert against hand-written EXPECTED_TOPOLOGY literals in python/synapse/validation/solaris/verify_*.py and cannot fail in response to the tool source they name. The F3 one additionally asserts the defect is STILL PRESENT while the live pin proves it repaired.
for_ruling.options: (a) re-aim each at the live graph, as SR1 did for the F4 live pin - Law 6's 'rewrite it to assert the behaviour at its real home'; (b) derive EXPECTED_TOPOLOGY from the tool's own plan() output so the literal cannot drift; (c) retire the static tier entirely now that the live tier exists and is mutation-proven.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I - a value judgement between defensible options, and the brief explicitly forbids this leg from quietly rewriting them. (b) is my recommendation: it keeps a cheap no-Houdini tier and makes drift structurally impossible.
for_ruling.note: Whichever is chosen, the F3 static pin is actively misleading TODAY: it encodes 'F3 is still broken' as a passing assertion.

for_ruling.question: Does the `pytest -k solaris` oracle clause mean the gate interpreter or the shipping interpreter?
for_ruling.context: 0 failed on the gate interpreter; 6 failed on the shipping interpreter, all six 'pytest-asyncio absent' (Q2 bucket 1, ENVIRONMENT, pre-existing, unrelated to Solaris). harness/supply_shipping_deps.ps1 exists and would close them.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Closing them means installing packages into the Houdini interpreter - changing the instrument mid-measurement. R47 already owns that intervention class. Sequencing judgement, not an agent's to take.

for_ruling.question: Ruling 15 retired `parent`, but PARENT_KEYS still accepts it as an alias, and _resolve_parent_path still silently defaults to /stage on an unknown key (H2b-F5).
for_ruling.context: import_megascans rejects unknown keys; component_builder does not. The convergence is real for the spelled keys and absent for the failure mode.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Whether 'retired' means removed or aliased is a product decision, and whether an unknown parent key should raise is a caller-contract decision that binds beyond Solaris.

for_ruling.question: The read-only fence for dispatched agents (H2b-F1).
for_ruling.context: Three attempts, three intrusions, despite escalating explicitness. Constitution Article V's worktree rule is necessary but was not sufficient - attempts 2 and 3 had their own worktrees and still wrote to the orchestrator's.
for_ruling.why_escalated: It is a harness-architecture decision and touches harness/agent-settings.json, which is deny-listed from agent edit - so it is a ruling item, not a permission problem (Article I corollary).
